readerContract.humanQuestion: How do I stop asking an AI to make a work draft vaguely better?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Turn taste into three visible checks, request one bounded revision and decide whether the work passes.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: The reader can use an approved workplace AI tool but does not know evaluation terminology.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: An AI can revise toward a visible finish line more usefully than toward an adjective, but the human still judges the real work.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A briefing note that looks polished but hides the decision, mismatches a figure or lacks an owner.
readerContract.surfaceJob: One compact work-facing Paige action, not a mini-class or news report.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: That is concrete enough to try on my next draft.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Either primary guide changes, the tip becomes a universal or provider-specific claim, or Paige's accepted lane changes.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Before another AI revision, replace better with three visible results the finished work must produce.
causalSequence: A vague quality word leaves the target unstated.
Three observable checks make the target visible.
The AI revises toward those checks.
The reader applies the same checks and verifies facts against approved sources.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A briefing note must name the decision in paragraph one, match the approved figures and show an owner and date.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A meeting summary must separate decisions from discussion, name each owner and preserve the agreed deadlines.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Write three checks, request one revision and compare the result yourself.

analogyPlan.mapping: The three visible checks define where the revision is trying to arrive.
analogyPlan.limit: Work quality has several dimensions and a finish line does not verify facts or fairness.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: It turns an invisible standard into something the reader can picture and test.

humourPlan.lessonJob: The trophy line makes the human-judgment boundary memorable without obscuring the action.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Recognizable work moment; exact action with a briefing-note example; plain cause; privacy and accuracy boundary; observable human result check; no continuation link.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No check-the-receipts lesson, no ceremonial mega-prompt, no provider-specific feature instructions and no Promptoscope humour frame.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Start with the failed work moment, make the invisible target visible, explain one cause and land on one human check.

humanQuestion.reason: The reader recognizes repeated vague revision requests.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: The first sentence names the polished-but-wrong work draft.

usefulCuriosity.reason: The reader needs to see why better is not an instruction.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: The mechanism contrasts an adjective with three observable results.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: The AI cannot infer the reader's unstated finish line reliably.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: The finish line becomes three things a person must be able to find or do.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: A briefing note makes the method concrete without technical jargon.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: The worked case names decision, figures, owner and date.

limitationsConsequences.reason: Criteria can be satisfied while facts still change.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: The adjacent boundary requires an approved tool, permitted material and source checks.

humourSurprise.reason: One trophy line reinforces human judgment.
humourSurprise.plannedEvidence: The AI does not award itself the trophy after revision.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The useful question is whether the reader can find or do each named thing.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: The final check asks exactly that.

explanationArc.adaptation: The 90-180 word service card answers immediately and uses only the explanatory moves needed for one action.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Repeating the overused check-the-receipts lesson or presenting a slogan instead of a followable method.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: The exact candidate must contain one work problem, one three-check action, the causal reason, an adjacent boundary and a human comparison test.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A non-technical reader can state what to write before the next revision and how to decide whether it helped.
